items.stem: Every significant decision in a fast-scaling firm is escalated to the two founders. What operating-model fix addresses the root cause?

options.text: Define and delegate clear decision rights so decisions are made at the right level
options.rationale: Correct: explicit, delegated decision rights relieve the founder bottleneck at its source.
Adding founders does not fix unclear decision rights.

options.text: Have the founders work longer hours
options.rationale: This treats a symptom, not the structural cause.

options.text: Stop making decisions until the firm is smaller
options.rationale: Not a viable or structural fix.

items.explanation: Correct: explicit, delegated decision rights relieve the founder bottleneck at its source.

items.stem: Which TWO signs most strongly indicate a company has outgrown its operating model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Decisions that used to be quick now stall and escalate
options.rationale: Correct: decision gridlock is a classic breakpoint symptom.

options.text: Coordination overhead and rework are rising sharply
options.rationale: Correct: rising coordination cost signals the model no longer fits the size.
Growth itself is not a sign of an outgrown model.

options.text: The company moved to a larger office
options.rationale: Office size is not an operating-model signal.
Branding is unrelated to operating-model fit.

items.explanation: Correct: decision gridlock is a classic breakpoint symptom.

items.stem: A scaling firm responds to chaos by adding approval steps and committees everywhere. What is the risk?

options.text: Premature bureaucracy slows decisions and erodes the speed that made the firm successful
options.rationale: Correct: over-processing too early trades away speed without solving the real structural gaps.

options.text: More approvals always improve decision quality
options.rationale: Excess approvals usually degrade speed and ownership.

options.text: Bureaucracy has no downside at scale
Committees remove the need for decision rights
options.rationale: They often blur, not clarify, decision rights.

items.explanation: Correct: over-processing too early trades away speed without solving the real structural gaps.
